design.latent_biological_null: Within every species, binary trait state is independent of local position before the observation process. Species baseline trait frequencies vary geographically among species.
design.mcar: Selection probability is independent of trait and local position.
design.trait_only: Selection probability depends on trait state only.
design.position_only: Selection probability depends on local position only.
design.joint_trait_position: Selection probability depends on the interaction between trait state and local position, so conditioning on observation can induce within-species trait-position association.

interpretation.supported: When the latent trait is spatially independent within species, species-conditioned matched-null inference remains near nominal rejection under MCAR, trait-only selection and position-only selection in this benchmark. When observation depends jointly on trait state and position, the observed sample itself acquires within-species trait-position association; both matched-null and species-fixed logistic analyses then reject frequently. Matched randomization calibrates inference conditional on the observed rows and sampling geometry, but cannot reconstruct or remove unmeasured outcome-by-location selection that changed which rows were observed.
not_supported: interpreting joint-selection rejection as a conventional type-I calibration failure conditional on the observed sample
claiming matched permutation can identify whether observed spatial organization is biological or selection-induced without additional observation-process information
claiming model-based fixed-effect logistic inference solves joint trait-by-position selection
claiming trait-only or position-only missingness is harmless under every data-generating process
